item.title: prix0rs the Cactus: Re: prix0rs the Cactus
item.content:encoded:
Hello! I am here per our IRC exchange to offer crit

Crit lives within
Yeeted and Deleeted

ConProcs

The temperature in its containment chamber is to be kept at a minimum of 28 degrees Celsius.

I would indicate which direction this errs. Is higher okay? Or is lower?

This is an otherwise very brief section so I have little to say. We just get right on into it and I'm good with that.

+++Description

Two arms extend from the central portion of its body.

Consider: "Two arms extend from center mass"

via levitation, usually at most 0.3 meters above the ground.

Language cleanup and significant digits. Consider: "levitation at an elevation of approximately 30cm"

SCP-XXXX is sentient and capable of speech via telepathy.

You might mean sapient. You might also want to say "communication via telepathy" rather than speech.

recording a corrupted version of its speech.

"corrupted version" is highly dubious.

It is capable of firing regular revolver ammunition

Since we just switched to the -1 I think it's probably fine, but, you could maybe stand to clarify the noun here a bit better in this passage.

bullets with a trajectory unaffected by wind,

Wind is only a factor at distances which are pretty well in excess of the range of a revolver.

It then traveled 6 kilometers across the city of Hollister,

I want to bring this up because the entire rest of this article is just one massive masquerade breach and you never cover or refer to that explicitly. There are "sightings" and nobody seems to call out the fact a levitating cactus is talking to them as it fights crime. If you want people to be nonplussed that is certainly an approach you can take, but we, as the Foundation, categorically should not be abiding this as "business as usual".

Video Logs

SCP-XXXX 'kicks' open the front door to a Starbucks.

This factually can't happen so I don't get why we're being coy. The door explodes inward, or, the door opens unassisted. This isn't very clinical even though I know exactly what you mean.

evaded capture for approximately 8 hours

This kind of begs the question of escalation. Why are we letting some random embedded agents chase this guy for a full day without sending help? Reduce the number, or send help.

technicians who smelled gunpowder in the water supply

I don't follow what this is implying and it never seems to come up again. You also probably wouldn't "smell" gunpowder; it only has a distinct smell when it's been fired/spent and that's not going to happen in water.

I liked the characterization of the video logs overall but I do have to warn you about your dialogue; you use a truly stupendous amount of exclamation points, and when they are so common they lose their meaning. Please strongly reconsider how you are applying this punctuation with an aim toward toning it down.

The best place to use an exclamation is after an interjection or command word. This is a way to suddenly or notably raise the level of emotion so you want to apply it rarely so people notice the departure from baseline. If every other line has an exclamation then that is a very excited and exhausting new baseline. I can clarify further if you want.

I would like to read this again to offer more thoughts as you explore the issues with the town, or alternatively, tighten up the timeline so those issues can be brushed away. As it stands, I am having trouble getting into what you're presenting because of the issues with the framework. I will say, in general, the central character does convey a good sense of identity but I think that their perseverance in the face of a less accommodating world might make them come through even more.

item.title: Need critique on a draft I made: Forum Criticism Team - Captain Post
item.content:encoded:
Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

Please first go to the Ideas forum or the chat, give a quick summary (for the Ideas forum, please follow the instructions in the required reading thread) of the concept you want to write up (don't link the draft unless someone requests it), and reviewers can help you make sure that your core idea is something that will be successful with the community audience.

During the conceptualization stage, reviewers can also help by letting you know if something similar already exists on the site, and/or telling you if there are any cliches/pitfalls/other typical downvote reasons to be careful of with your particular idea. These issues are more effectively addressed earlier on in the writing process.

If you have already received the requisite greenlights, please note from whom and where you received them. If you would like to receive draft critique without going through the greenlighting process, please use the IRC chatrooms to request reviews.

item.title: Monstrous teeth: Re: Monstrous teeth
item.content:encoded:
Hey there. I'm a newbie here so I don't know much, but after looking through this Drafts Critique forum for a while, I noticed a rule that the admins keep posting.

Then again you said you are not a first-time author, so I don't know if this applies to you, but here is the comment I copied from a senior member:

Author, per the Draft Forum's new policy: http://www.scp-wiki.net/forum/t-10629348/new-draft-forum-policies authors who have not yet posted a successful mainsite article are now required to get their basic concept(s) greenlighted by two experienced reviewers in the Ideas Critique forum and/or IRC chatrooms before asking for draft feedback.

You already have a thread for this here: http://www.scpwiki.com/forum/t-13855933/therapist-based-scp so I suggest reaching out to reviewers to ask them to look at that thread so you can obtain the necessary greenlights to get draft critique here.

That's about it.

Also, my personal opinion on this SCP: it would scare the living cr*p out of me. However, I do not understand the reason for it being Keter class. It does not kill or otherwise harm SCP-XXXX-2. You did mention at the end that he is not dangerous but his modus operandi is disturbing, however I would still, personally, make it a Euclid class.

Also, what would happen exactly if it were not allowed to treat a D-class daily? How would it try to breach containment?

Lastly, I don't think the Foundation would go out of their way to call it Dr SCP-XXXX simply because of it requesting it.

As it's stated in the How to Write an SCP page: Don't write its containment procedures to essentially be "Give it What it Wants". The Foundation is not a hotel, it is a prison.

Thus, I highly doubt the Foundation would grant this SCP's request to be called Doctor.

item.title: The thrilling world of Foundation bureaucracy: Re: The thrilling world of Foundation bureaucracy
item.content:encoded:
Was asked to take a look at this. Expect crit within 24 hours.

Yes, this is very snappy. The prose and the writing are all generally tight in a way I can really enjoy, barring the occasional absented space or "SCP-XXX".

I think that my biggest issue with the draft is just the fact that the object is wholy mundane, which makes justifying the ensuing O5 involvement and Ethics Committee involvement difficult. The object in question is just Procrastinati or any other antimeme, and not a particularly effective one at that. I think I'd care more about the story if there were some element about the rock that was intriguing/unexplained on its own, or presented some (perhaps negligible) threat. There's also the concern that there's no real satisfying or implied conclusion for this thing's origins — perhaps, again, due to the mundanity of its effect.

There's also just… something about that image. I don't know. I've never been a fan of pictures with totally white backgrounds — it feels very inauthentic.

To address your concerns in the top post — everything seems to stay its welcome pretty well, barring the one section listing off the previous owners. I feel like the candidate list could be downsized somewhat.

item.title: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification: Form 1004-E: Proposal for Reclassification
item.content:encoded:
http://scp-sandbox-3.wikidot.com/deathbygin-2

A short tale for my authored article SCP-5118.

Spoiler / Explanation
Minimize

As Dr. Atmos gather information from Dr. Williams, it's implied that SCP-5118 is actually a dog who is a reality bender, turned human, and turned back into a dog when about to be captured. Evidence to support this includes:

  • SCP-5118 did not act like most other reality benders do when discovering they have powers (usually by hiding them from others).
  • SCP-5118 manifests chocolate, grapes, and soda - all things a dog cannot eat.
  • SCP-5118 appeared to be smiling while being chased.
  • SCP-5118 does not attempt to breach containment because it's current living situation is already ideal (it gets a bed, new toys, guaranteed food and water, and socializes with staff daily when they provide it with food).
  • Using it's powers while in containment would risk exposing itself. Since it's implied that it's "original form" is already a dog, the scans / tests from the SCP article would show nothing.

I wanted to write this tale to add a twist to the article without making this the clear-cut canon. Please let me know what you think.
